questions.question: Why is 'cost per interaction' an essential metric for AI product business health, beyond typical engagement metrics?
options: It isn't important; engagement metrics alone are always sufficient
Every AI interaction has a real, calculable cost, and growing usage without cost context can mean growing losses rather than growing success
Cost per interaction only matters for features with fewer than 100 users
AI features never have any meaningful cost per interaction
questions.explanation: Since AI interactions have real, measurable costs (tied to token economics), understanding cost per interaction relative to the value generated is essential to knowing whether rising usage reflects a sustainable, profitable feature or a growing financial liability.

questions.question: What is 'deflection rate' (or containment rate) and why does it matter for support-oriented AI features?
options: The percentage of users who stop using a feature entirely
The percentage of interactions fully resolved by the AI without human intervention, directly tied to the feature's cost-saving value proposition
The speed at which a model generates its first token
A measure of how many tokens a request uses
questions.explanation: For AI features designed to reduce human workload, deflection rate measures how many interactions are actually resolved without escalating to a human, which is often the core metric tied to the feature's business value.

questions.question: A team reports '50,000 daily interactions and rising' as evidence their AI chatbot feature is succeeding. Which question best challenges this claim?
options: Should we just accept rising usage as proof of success?
What is the cost per interaction and quality score alongside this usage growth — could rising interactions reflect users re-asking due to unsatisfying answers rather than genuine value?
Should we increase the feature's usage target even higher?
Is this metric measured in the correct time zone?
questions.explanation: Engagement alone is ambiguous — it could reflect genuine value or a broken, frustrating experience generating repeated re-attempts. Cost and quality metrics are needed alongside engagement to distinguish between these very different underlying realities.
